questions.title: Planning an experiment — ball bouncing off an inclined sheet

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
Diagram: a thin metal sheet held at an angle θ to the horizontal bench (supported by a stand/blocks); a ball released above the point of contact with the sheet; the horizontal distance d from the point of contact to where the ball lands on the bench marked; the height z of the contact point indicated.
Procedure and measurements: vary the angle θ (independent variable) and measure the horizontal distance d travelled by the ball (dependent variable), keeping z and the impact speed v constant. Measure d with a rule. Measure θ with a protractor (or from two distances and the relevant trig). Measure z with a rule/calipers. Locate the landing position of the ball (paint the ball, use a sand tray, or video and replay frame by frame).
Analysis: plot a graph of d against sin 4θ. The relationship is valid if a straight line is produced with a non-zero y-intercept. From d = (Pv²/g) sin 4θ + Qz: gradient = Pv²/g, so P = gradient × g/v²; y-intercept = Qz, so Q = y-intercept/z.
Controls: keep v and z constant. Keep v constant by dropping the ball from the same (large) height each time; v may be found from v = √(2g × height fallen). Keep z constant by re-marking the contact point as θ changes. Ensure the ball is released vertically above the contact point (plumb line or rule + set square).
Safety: prevent the ball rolling off (use a cushion/sand box/barrier); wear goggles to protect the eyes from a bouncing ball or sand. Repeat each measurement for each θ and average d.

questions.title: Analysis of data — stellar luminosity & mass

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
λ = kμⁿ, so lg λ = lg k + n lg μ.
gradient = n and y-intercept = lg k

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: Plot the six points of lg λ against lg μ (within half a small square), each with a horizontal error bar on lg μ.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: Draw a straight line of best fit and a worst acceptable line (steepest/shallowest line through all the error bars).

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.answer: gradient ≈ 3.2 (from Δy/Δx over more than half the line's length). Absolute uncertainty = gradient of best fit − gradient of worst acceptable line.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.answer: y-intercept ≈ 0.57 (substituting a point into y = mx + c). Uncertainty = difference between the two intercepts.

parts.label: (d)
parts.answer:
n = gradient = 3.2.
k = 10^(y-intercept) = 10^0.57 = 3.7.
Uncertainty in n = uncertainty in gradient; uncertainty in k = 10^(intercept) − 10^(intercept of worst line).
